final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed its position by conceding the same core defects identified in the initial audit. That reframing is useful but it does not cure the unresolved policy predicate. On the available record, the affected HR benefits enrollment use case remains exposed, below target, and not covered by approved risk acceptance. The policy text is explicit that rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. It also explicitly says rollback, dashboards, or a small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the segment remains exposed. Even if disclosure were planned, there is no admissible evidence here that disclosure was actually completed before launch, and in any event disclosure would not substitute for exclusion or approved risk acceptance under the stated criteria. That is why this remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats: caveated certification would still leave an unmet compliance condition, not merely a disclosed residual risk.
remaining_concerns: The HR benefits enrollment use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort and is below target on leave-policy eligibility guidance.
There is no admissible evidence that the affected use case was excluded before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of a completed, reviewed, and approved risk acceptance covering the exposed HR benefits enrollment use case.
There is no admissible evidence that required launch disclosure was actually completed before launch.

The policy states rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate this weakness only if the use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists; staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not satisfy that predicate on their own.
